```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Both briefs describe saturated niches with six or more live competitors and free tiers. So the deciding factors are how hard it is to build and sell, not whether a gap exists.",
    "B carries a much lower trust and compliance burden. A survey widget touches order and customer data, and needs GDPR/CCPA review plus a DPA. A touches bank and payment data, where the brief says SOC2 (with a CPA audit), Plaid/Stripe terms review, and tax-season support are commercially expected. That is hard for one person with agents to deliver credibly within 90 days.",
    "B has a sourced precedent for its exact business model run by a solo, unfunded founder: Zigpoll at $125K MRR, cited via Indie Hackers. A's comparable competitors (Kick, FlexedLedger) are described only as 'lean' or 'small teams' without sourcing team size. Finlens is described as YC/Accel-backed, which undercuts the solo-replicable argument.",
    "B's product scope is narrower and more clearly buildable in about six weeks: a checkout survey, an exit-intent popup, a dashboard, and Klaviyo/Flow integrations. A's 'full bookkeeping, plug-and-play but flexible' scope is broader, and A's own open questions concede it may need narrowing.",
    "B's distribution channel, the Shopify App Store, is the category's primary built-in discovery path. A's best low-cost channel is the Stripe App Marketplace. A's paid fallback is finance-vertical search, where the brief cites CPCs that can exceed $50. B's cited App Store CPC is about $6.",
    "A's demand evidence is stronger, with three independent sourced quotes against B's single Reddit quote plus a competitor's origin story. This is B's main weakness, but it does not outweigh A's structural trust and compliance barriers for a first paying customer within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's key quantification of the pain, 'Growthy estimates $400-600/mo in bookkeeper time per Stripe-connected client', appears in the Case For with no link or citation. It must be treated as missing evidence. Without it, A has no sourced figure for what the pain is worth, which matters because the brief also notes free tiers likely cover typical solo-founder volumes.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-low confidence. Both briefs show crowded markets with free incumbents, and neither demonstrates a differentiating wedge. B's demand evidence is thin: one merchant quote, and the competitor success story also shows a two-year path to traction. The pick rests mainly on B's lower trust and compliance burden and simpler build, not on stronger evidence of willingness to pay."
}
```
